newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK SHARES END FIRM IN THIN TRADING.
newsitem.headline: GREEK SHARES END FIRM IN THIN TRADING.

text.p: Greek stocks edged 0.70 percent forward on Monday, helped by upbeat industrial stocks and a late surge in OTE telecom in an otherwise low volume dull session.

"Equities have stabilised within a tight trading range in the face of a halt in the flow of positive news from the macroeconomy and the money market, including a blip in short interbank rates and a rigid inflation rate," said Filippos Boukouvalas, fund manager at Kosmos SoGen mutual funds.
"But unless the market is dealt with serious adverse news, there is limited downside risk at current price levels," he added.
A Reuters poll of 15 bankers and economists produced a mean and median 5.4 percent forecast for Greek consumer inflation in June, unchanged from May.
The market was seen remaining rangebound in the near-term, though prospects for the coming months were brighter as new market-moving developments were expected to unfold.

"It will probably be a quiet July for equities, but thereafter the market will be affected by first half corporate results and expectations on the outcome of the September decision for the 2004 Olympics," Boukouvalas said.
The city of Athens, along with Rome, are the main candidates for hosting the 2004 Olympic games which are expected to necessitate a fair amount of infrastructure works.
The Athens general index settled 0.72 percent or 10.84 points higher at 1,518.51 from Friday's 1,507.67, recovering from an intra-day low of 1,504.91.
Industrials gained 0.73 percent leading the market along with OTE telecom which firmed 3.95 percent, outweighing a 0.20 percent drop in banks. Other sectors were mixed.
Turnover was slack, reaching a mere 18.1 billion drachmas on volume of 4.2 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 117 to 88 with 31 shares unchanged on 235 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $11.30-$11.75. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,102-1,132 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,060-1,120 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying instrument were up 75 drachmas to 6,280.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 572.68-609.24 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $64.68-$66.37. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,052-3,266 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $9.40-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 196-227 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
